in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with the basics: **Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 9 years old and lives with me at home. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Your son Alex is 9 years old and lives with you - that's a good start.

Now I need to ask: **Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! You live in the UK with Alex in Manchester.

Next question: **Are you the person primarily responsible for Alex's care? This typically means you're the one providing for his day-to-day needs like food, clothes, and general upkeep.**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm the one who looks after him day-to-day - I provide his meals, buy his clothes, take care of all his needs. He lives with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, that's very clear. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another family member?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. One more important question:

**Do you or your partner (if you have one) have an individual income over £60,000 per year?** 

(This won't affect your eligibility, but it may mean you have to pay a High Income Child Benefit tax charge, so it's important to be aware of.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't have information about my income in my circumstances, so I'm not sure about that. Is that something that would stop me from being eligible?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's perfectly fine - thank you for letting me know. The good news is that **income does NOT affect your eligibility for Child Benefit**. You can still claim it regardless of your income level.

The income question is only relevant for the High Income Child Benefit tax charge (which applies if you or a partner earn over £60,000), but that's a separate tax matter and doesn't prevent you from being eligible or claiming.

Based on the information you've provided:
- Alex is 9 years old (under 16)
- He lives with you in the UK
- You're responsible for his day-to-day care
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him

Let me provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You ARE eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the requirements:
- ✓ Alex is under 16 years old
- ✓ You live in the UK
- ✓ You're responsible for Alex's care and he lives with you
- ✓ Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him

You can go ahead and make a claim for Child Benefit. If you haven't already claimed, you should do so as soon as possible, as Child Benefit can only be backdated for up to 3 months from the date you claim.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or the claiming process?
